name: blast-execution-visual
description: Visual verification of blast execution and effects: explosion animation, energy propagation visualization, fragment spawning, projection flyrock, Tier A projected vs Tier B collapse physics, and PHYSICS_FRAGMENT_CAP overflow fallback

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from $50,000 to $3,000,000 -- this file drills+blasts 4 separate times, each cycle now needing its own driller+drill_rig ($36,000) on top of payroll/upkeep during 4 drilling waits, and the 4th cycle restores its pre-#553 rows:8 cols:8 (64-hole) grid -- required by tests/unit/scenario-defs-blast-visual-coverage.test.ts to stress the projectile-grouping path (#404) -- which a single driller/drill_rig takes over 1000 ticks to land door-to-door even at tight spacing:1.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so each of this file's 4 blast cycles needs its own fresh crew (this employee is fired again right after its blast, see below, so an idle survivor from an earlier cycle never drags the roster's average wellbeing down -- sandbox-measured: leaving prior staffed employees idle for the whole ~400-tick file causes a genuine worker_revolt by cycle 4, regardless of how light any single cycle's own workload is).

#928: the single-gauge fatigue model concentrates all morale damage into fatigue alone, so a driller working continuously with nowhere to rest (NEED_REST_NO_BUILDING_CAP=70, double duration with no building in range) tanks well-being to a sustained 0 and triggers a genuine worker_revolt well before this file's actual blast-execution assertions are reached (sandbox-measured: by tick ~380, inside the very first drill/blast cycle). A living_quarters lets collapse-rest fully replenish fatigue in normal time instead of capping/doubling it, keeping well-being off the revolt floor for the rest of this ~1000-tick file. Placed in a far corner (2,58), deliberately clear of grid centre (32,32) -- every purchased vehicle spawns staggered outward from grid centre (VehiclePlacement's own spawn-ring logic), and this file's cycle-4 8x8 grid alone buys 8 more rigs into that same small cluster; a living_quarters footprint dropped into that cluster (sandbox-confirmed at 32,32) walls off some of those tightly packed spawn tiles from each other, and the drillers assigned to them go permanently isMoveStuck trying to board -- a real dispatch/pathing defect (any obstacle shares this risk when dropped into that cluster, not something specific to this building type), tracked as a follow-up rather than fixed here since this file only needs to place the building somewhere that isn't the vehicle spawn cluster. Also clear of every cycle's own hole grid (20,20 / 45,20 / 5,5 / 59,59).
#928: let the driller hired above walk over and finish building the living_quarters before cycle 1's drill_plan sends it off to the first hole grid.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.description: Grid 1/4. The spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts); one decrement click lowers it to 2 before dragging, so the (20,20)-(22,22) rectangle (2x2) computes the declared 2x2 at spacing:2 (issue #479 follow-up, Finding #4). Spacing stays at 2 afterward — it persists across grid operations within a session, so grids 2-4 below inherit it (grid 4/4 decrements it further, down to 1). depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper, so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default. Only hole/charge/sequence counts are asserted anywhere in this file (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction. #553: shrunk from 3x3 (9 holes) to 2x2 (4 holes) and spacing tightened to 2m -- a single driller cannot land this file's original 9+4+4+64=81 total holes across 4 cycles without a genuine worker_revolt (sandbox-measured); the interaction array's spacing-stepper click and drag rectangle below now match this declared shape.

#928: was a flat `tick 50`, sized for a driller who starts drilling at tick 0. This file's own living_quarters build (above) now runs the driller through a walk-and-build detour first, so cycle 1's drilling no longer starts at a fixed tick -- wait_until (#590) drives to actual completion instead of a hand-measured pad, matching cycles 2-4's own pattern below.

#554/#590 finding: charging is real, worker-performed work that can take long enough (relative to MIN_EVENT_INTERVAL_TICKS) for a spontaneous event to fire mid-wait -- a single long `waitUntil` has no way to resolve one in interaction mode (its real, isPaused-gated clock halts exactly as it would for a real player, per interaction-executor.ts's own waitUntil doc comment), so the drain stalls forever at whatever count was ordered when the event hit. Command mode's own waitUntil auto-resolves silently and never showed this. Chunked here into the same tick-N/event-choose-0 pattern already used for this file's drilling waits, which does resolve mid-wait events in both modes.

The added `wait`+`assert` pair below is the one place in this file that waits a flat real-time duration rather than polling a condition: there is no DOM-observable signal for "the collapse is still mid-flight" other than the report modal's own closed state, which is exactly what that assert checks, so the wait exists only to create the checkpoint moment the assert reads.

expect.note: #950: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero — CATASTROPHIC rating with real projections confirms this grid's overcharge/understemmed premise actually holds at the UI-reachable stemming floor, not just at the command's old unreachable stemming:0. The report modal must still be closed at t=3200ms (past the old fixed 3000ms floor, per the assert above) while this real collapse is still playing, only opening once the awaitUsable step above proves it genuinely did, and closed again (this `blocked` goal) by the real CLOSE click at the end of this step's own interaction array.

Necessary but not sufficient on its own for grid 4's revolt -- see the charge-relief hires further down this file's own note for the other half of the fix.

#586 CI real root cause (live-state confirmed, not the stuck-report-modal theory): grid 4's single driller/drill_rig from #553 keeps working this whole ~1000-tick wait with nothing ever restoring its morale to the "comfortable"(>=50) band needsMoraleEffect (EmployeeNeeds.ts) requires just to stop draining -- avgMorale clamps to 0 by roughly tick 400, dragging state.scores.wellBeing (ScoreManager.ts) to 0 with it, and WorkerRevolt.ts ends the level for real (levelEndReason:'worker_revolt') once that holds for REVOLT_TICKS (120, balance.ts) -- confirmed live via window.__gameState()/__uiState() at the failing step: the toolbar was covered by #bs-level-end-screen, not any blast-report overlay. Sandbox-tested fix: 7 more drillers (8 total) on Tier-3 drill_rigs (VEHICLE_TIER_MULTIPLIERS workRate x2.0/speed x1.8, balance.ts) parallelize the 64-hole plan below to done (orderedHoleCount:0) by tick ~421 -- about 150 ticks of margin before revolt would fire at ~571 in the same sandboxed run -- letting the tick-150 wait round below (now 2, not 7) end this grid before wellBeing ever finishes crashing, instead of racing it. Building a Tier-2+ living_quarters was tried and rejected: it enables GameLoop.ts's processShiftCycle, but WORK_DURATION_TICKS is only 6 -- every driller within its search radius spends most of its time walking to and from the bunkhouse rather than drilling, and holeCount actually stalled at 3/64. Firing and re-hiring the driller mid-grid was also tried and rejected: fireEmployee (Employee.ts) refuses a unionized employee (30% chance per hire, Employee.ts's rng.chance(0.3)), and this seed unionizes id4 on its very first roll, so every fire attempt no-ops and each replacement hire only adds another employee dragging the roster average once it, too, crashes. Interaction-mode fix: this and the remaining grid-4 filler hires (50, 53, 56, 59, 62, 65) switched from `equals` on an absolute employeeCount to `changedBy: {employeeCount: 1}`, matching the pattern steps 14/27/44 already established for grid 2/3/4's own first hire. Root cause, confirmed directly (command mode: employee #1 survives its own grid-1 blast and gets properly fired, employeeCount:1 going into grid 2; real interaction mode: employee #1 instead dies in that same blast -- this file's own already-accepted "No-op if the employee already died in its own blast" case for the fire step, just landing the other way around from grid-1's own die-vs-survive coin flip than command mode's) -- a dead employee is never spliced from the roster (only a real fire does that), so which baseline grid 4's hires start counting up from is real, mode-dependent, and outside this step's own control. Same class of divergence vibration-budget.json's own history already found and fixed the same way (dropping `employeeCount` from that file's own equals block, scenario-defs.md's own changedBy convention for a field a legitimate per-mode split makes non-deterministic).

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:8 cols:8 spacing:1 depth:6 start:5,5
steps.description: Grid 4/4. #553 restores this file's original 8x8 (64 holes) grid -- required by tests/unit/scenario-defs-blast-visual-coverage.test.ts's own coverage regression guard (#404), which locks in a rows:8/cols:8 grid to exceed MAX_ACTIVE_PROJECTILES (256, balance.ts) and exercise the projectile-grouping path once heavily overcharged below. Spacing tightened to 1m (two decrement clicks off the 2m spacing inherited from grids 1-3; the second click is a no-op against the 1m floor, but the first alone would already suffice) so the drag only spans (5,5)-(12,12) -- 8 parallel drillers (see above) clear it in ~2 tick-150 rounds instead of 1 driller needing over 1000 ticks door-to-door, which is what made this grid's wellbeing crash unrecoverable in the first place (#586 CI).

#586 CI real root cause (live-state confirmed, not the stuck-report-modal theory): grid 4's tick-150 wait used to run 7 rounds here so a SINGLE driller could door-to-door drill all 64 holes -- that ~1000-tick uninterrupted stretch is what crashed state.scores.wellBeing (ScoreManager.ts) to 0 and held it there past REVOLT_TICKS (120), ending the level for real via WorkerRevolt.ts (levelEndReason:'worker_revolt') before this file's own charge/sequence/blast steps ever ran -- confirmed live via window.__gameState()/__uiState() at the failing step: the toolbar was covered by #bs-level-end-screen, not any blast-report overlay. Sandbox-tested (both pure command-mode and live interaction-mode): every driller headcount and vehicle tier tried still lets the SAME crash reach revolt by tick ~571 measured from new_game -- more drillers/faster rigs raise the drilled-hole count somewhat by this point but never reach all 64 before that deadline, and a living_quarters (which would let employees recover) sends them on round trips that stall drilling even worse than the crash does. Reduced from 7 rounds to 2 (this is the last one) so the wait stops here, at tick ~421, a comfortable ~150 ticks before the revolt threshold, and the charge/sequence/blast steps below run against however many of the 64 holes 8 parallel Tier-3-rig drillers manage to finish by then (was 64/64 with the single-driller design; is well over half now, still far more than enough to exceed MAX_ACTIVE_PROJECTILES (256, balance.ts) once heavily overcharged) rather than gambling the run on finishing literally all 64 before wellbeing running out.

#682: first of 24 charge-only relief hires -- deliberately never assigned driving.drill_rig or any vehicle, so TaskDispatch can never route them to a drill_hole action (which requires a drill_rig). Every driller role starts with 'blasting' at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), which is all charge_hole requires (requiredVehicleRole: null, dispatchChargeAction/mining.ts) -- these 24 exist purely to parallelize loading the ~61 holes the 8 working drillers above landed. Direct trace (issue #682): charging that many 8kg holes with only the 8 working drillers (who by this point are also blasting-qualified and free once their own drilling plateaus, per the tick-150 steps above) took long enough under set_policy's own forced-rest interruptions that wellBeing's zero-streak still crossed REVOLT_TICKS during the charge-drain wait below. 24 more (cheap, $1000 each, no vehicle purchase) cut that phase from 300+ ticks to well under 120 -- sandbox-confirmed: charging finishes at ticksAtZero=41, comfortably under the 120-tick threshold, where 8-only and even 16-with-vehicles crews (both tried and rejected, see git history) still crossed it. Hired AFTER the drilling wait above (not before) so none of them can accidentally have driving.drill_rig assigned to them by a later step meant for a working driller, and so they add no drilling-side congestion to the already-plateaued 8x8 grid.
